### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/rest_api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RestApiConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/rest_api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6b44efa7b4a429994dc6d92c3de96392d4e03f3f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c59414d9a56719bcd050a2679df8340e6d70dd09` — the merge of head `32bfe10cda2f5fdec1be6233b6f45e013ab256f6` into base `6b44efa7b4a429994dc6d92c3de96392d4e03f3f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c59414d9a56719bcd050a2679df8340e6d70dd09 && git checkout c59414d9a56719bcd050a2679df8340e6d70dd09
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6b44efa7b4a429994dc6d92c3de96392d4e03f3f 32bfe10cda2f5fdec1be6233b6f45e013ab256f6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6b44efa7b4a429994dc6d92c3de96392d4e03f3f && git merge --no-ff 32bfe10cda2f5fdec1be6233b6f45e013ab256f6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6b44efa7b4a429994dc6d92c3de96392d4e03f3f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6b44efa7b4a429994dc6d92c3de96392d4e03f3f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `32bfe10cda2f5fdec1be6233b6f45e013ab256f6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.rest-api-config-dead-keys-retired.ts + packages/rest/src/discovery-routes.ts (`registerOpenApiEndpoints`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`registerRoutes` gate), packages/spec/src/api/rest-api-config-dead-keys-retirement.test.ts (`DOCS_ENABLED_PRESCRIPTION`), packages/rest/src/rest-api-config-dead-keys-refused.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-docs-viewer-retired.pin.test.ts, content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx (regenerated from the describe), packages/spec/liveness/rest_api.json

Face: published schema (`rest-server.zod.ts`). Inputs read: card #25121 body and all four comments (two pointers, the claim, the os-dev-report), PR #25162 body, file list and net diff against `main` at this head, the 39 check-runs on the head, and the cited code as committed blobs at the head. Not read: the dispatch order or any seat's own conclusions. The remainder of the diff (`.changeset/25121-spec-openapi-viewer-prose.md`, `content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx`, `packages/spec/liveness/rest_api.json`, `packages/spec/scripts/lib/openapi-self-consistency.ts`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; it is read here only where a hunk in scope makes a claim about it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`RestApiConfigSchema.enableOpenApi` describe** — RIGHT. The published JSON-schema `description` string changes; the type (`boolean`), default (`true`) and key set do not, so the accept set is unchanged. The one tracked carrier of the describe text is `content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx`, regenerated in this diff (two table rows); a tree-wide search at the head finds the new text in exactly those two files and the old text ("Enable OpenAPI 3.1 spec & docs viewer endpoints", "Scalar-rendered") in no tracked file outside the changeset that quotes it and the release-owned changelogs. `gen:schema` reporting no tracked change is consistent with that.
2. **`enableOpenApi` TSDoc** — RIGHT. Published declaration docblock only; no type moves. Its claim — one endpoint, `GET BASEPATH/openapi.json` — is true of the cited code: `registerRoutes` gates `registerOpenApiEndpoints` on `api.enableOpenApi` (`rest-server.ts:4752`), and `registerOpenApiEndpoints` in `discovery-routes.ts` makes exactly one `routeManager.register` call, for path `BASEPATH/openapi.json`; its header records the `GET BASEPATH/docs` viewer as retired (#25104). `rest-docs-viewer-retired.pin.test.ts` pins both halves on both route shapes.
3. **`documentation.enabled` tombstone prescription** — RIGHT, and an accept-set no-op as the PR states. Same key refused, same `retiredKey()` tombstone, same issue path `documentation.enabled` / `api.documentation.enabled`, same `invalid_type` code, same opening sentence; only the closing clause changed. Both pins that read the message end their match at "`api.enableOpenApi: false` is the switch" (`DOCS_ENABLED_PRESCRIPTION` in the spec test, line 61; the rest test, line 101), which the new text keeps, so neither pin needed a flip and neither was touched. The new clause ("leaves the `/openapi.json` document unmounted") is what the rest pin measures at lines 198–204: with `enableOpenApi: false` the only route removed is `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`.
4. **Semantic entry 18 `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria`** — RIGHT. `id` and `surface` are unchanged, so the ADR-0087 registry key and the four ledger keys it covers are unchanged; only the prose `os migrate meta` and the generated upgrade guide show moved. "sees `GET /openapi.json` unmounted" is the same measured fact as item 3. `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` is a pointer, not a generated copy, so no tracked artifact of this entry is stale.
5. **Liveness `rest_api.json` evidence (claimed by the prescription hunk)** — RIGHT. "mounts `/openapi.json`, the OpenAPI document" matches the single registration in item 2; `verifiedAt` restamped to 2026-10-22 with the status still `live` and the producer unchanged. The head's `Spec property liveness` check-run is `success`.
6. **`openapi-self-consistency.ts` comment and refusal text** — RIGHT. Gate-script prose and a refusal message, not a published surface; the one consumer it now names (`GET /api/v1/openapi.json`) is the one that exists. `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` is `success` on the head.
7. **Public-surface summary** — no export added, removed or moved; no key added, removed or re-typed; no default changed; no refusal added or lifted. The diff publishes description text on `@objectstack/spec` only. The sweep claim in the report ("no further site in `packages/spec`") holds at the head: the remaining `/docs`-shaped hits in `packages/spec` are `content/docs` paths, the `docs.objectstack.dev` error URL and the two out-of-scope schemas (`ApiTestingUiConfigSchema`, `OpenApiGenerationConfigSchema.uiPath`), which the claim excludes and the card marks "noted, not decided".

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25121-spec-openapi-viewer-prose.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, carrying `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial; the PR body carries the same two lines. Judged against the diff: nothing an author can write is added, refused, tightened or re-meant, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is the kind, and `none` takes `patch` under AGENTS.md's level rule. `Clause-②: no` is TRUE — neither arm applies: the accept set of `RestApiConfigSchema` is identical before and after (item 3 is the only hunk on a refusal, and it changes the message's last clause only). `skip-changeset` would have been wrong: a released package's published description text moves. `Check Changeset` on the head is `success`. The changeset body carries no migration and owes none.

Clause-②: no — matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` — the PR body opens with an HTML-comment attribution line (`claude-projects-attribution`) while os-dev.md forbids HTML comments in GitHub text. Which governs?** Answered: **A**, keep it. os-dev.md's clause (lines 18 and 322–326) guards two things: seat markers the PM scans for, and the sanitizer eating tag-shaped fragments through to the end of the body. Neither bit here. The line is the dispatch relay's platform attribution, not a seat marker; the relay's read-back stored the body byte-identical (5797 sent, 5797 stored); and the two line-initial declarations after it parsed, since `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are both `success` on the head. Nothing in this repo (AGENTS.md, `scripts/`, `.github/`) requires or names that line, so the clause's wording is os-dev.md's owner to settle; escalated as a note, not a defect of this PR.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` ×3** — acknowledged, none blocks. The two ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove candidates (`ApiTestingUiConfigSchema` as `ApiDocumentationConfigSchema.ui`; `OpenApiGenerationConfigSchema.uiPath`) are retirements, a `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` the claim excluded and the card left undecided; the seat files them as their own card, correctly. `.changeset/25077-rest-docs-viewer-attr-escape.md` describes a fix to the page #25124 retired; release-owned input, correctly untouched here, and the release compiler should read it beside #25124.
- **Local `NOT MEASURED` families** — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, workspace unbuilt) is CI-owned under the Lint lanes; `check:dev-prereqs` reports the box's unbuilt state and names no stale spec dist. Both are the head's check-runs' to answer, not a local re-run's.
- **Docs Drift Check (PR comment 6331671865)** — `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx` names `RestApiConfigSchema`; release-owned, read-only, no edit owed by this PR. `packages/spec/liveness/rest_api.json` yielded no anchor; that file is item 5 above and the liveness check-run covers it.
- **Check-runs on the head (39):** 23 `success` (among them `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Type Check · source gates`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`); 6 `skipped` (opt-in or conditional: 18.x upgrade harness, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance); 16 **pending** at read time (`Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Test Core` 1–6, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`). Not waited for. This record judges the contract; the queue guard still owes the remaining gates their green before the PR lands, and a red among them is a lane finding, not a contract one, given a diff of description, TSDoc, comment and prescription text only.
